, or mutoraHN , accord. to different copies of the K, (TA,) One who ceases not to hear and see that which does not please him. (K.)

[ A cause of grief, sorrow, unhappiness, or anxiety: pl. mataAriHu . Hence the saying,] tar~aHatohu AlmataAriHu [ Misfortunes (lit. the causes of grief, &c.,) grieved him, or made him sorrowful, &c.]. (A.)

Strait, difficult, or distressful, life. (A, K.) ― -b2- A scanty torrent, or flow of water, in which is a stopping, or an interruption. (K.) -A2- A garment, or piece of cloth, dyed so as to be saturated with the dye. (Az, K.)
A she-camel whose milk soon comes to an end, or stops: (S, L:) pl. mataAriyHu . (L.)

[ A shield; ] a certain piece of defensive armour; (M, TA;) a thing well known: (A, Msb, K:) pl. tirasapN and tiraAsN (S, M, Msb, K) and tiraAsapN (S) and turuwsN , [all pls. of mult.,] and A^atoraAsN , [a pl. of pauc.,] (S, M, Msb, K,) but not A^atorisapN . (A, * TA.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A smooth, round, level piece of ground: (A, TA:) or a rugged piece of hard, or hard and level, ground. (Ibn- 'Abbád, K.) ― -b4- See also matarosN .

; so accord. to El-Háfidh Ibn-Hajar, and this is the correct form; written in the T and the Towsheeh mat~arosN ; and by some, matorasN [as in the CK]; and by some, matorasN [as I find it in two copies of the S and in a copy of the K]; (TA;) [ A wooden door-bar; ] a piece of wood that is put behind the door; (S, K) the $ijaAr [or wooden bar ] that is put against the door as a stay: (T, L, TA:) [ mataroso is] a Persian word, [having the above-mentioned signification, but originally a contraction of maho taroso , and] meaning “ fear not thou,” with it [being here understood]: (T, K, TA:) or the name of this piece of wood in Arabic is ↓ : (M, TA:) which also signifies a piece of wood with which a couch-frame ( sariyr ) is repaired, by its being affixed as a Dab~ap : (M:) [and the Arabic word $

, (M, A,) or mtorasapN , (K, accord. to the TA, [and so I find in a MS. copy of that work, and in the CK, but the former is probably the correct form, being agreeable with analogy, like maboxalapN and majobanapN &c.,]) Anything by which one is defended, or protected. (Lth, in TA. [But it is said in the TA, in one place, that Lth ignored the verb in this sense; and in another place, that he said, I have not heard them say, tariEa AlA_inaA='u .]) -A2- He hastened to do evil, or mischief; (Ks, K;) and to do a thing: (TA:) and bahi A_ilaY Al$~ar~i ↓ , accord. to the K; but accord. to the S and O and L, ↓ A_ilayohi biAl$~ar~i ; (TA;) he hastened to him to do evil, or mischief. Full; applied to a watering-trough or tank for beasts &c.; (S, K;) and to a mug: (S:) an inf. n. used as an epithet: (TA:) the regular form is ↓ , which signifies the same. (K.)

: see taraEN . ― -b2- Also A cloud containing much rain. (TA.) ― -b3- Eu$obN tariEN Fresh, juicy, or sappy, herbs or herbage. (Sgh in art. drE , and L.) -A2- A man quick to do evil, or mischief, (Ks, S,) and to become angry: (S:) ready and quick to become angry: and ↓ evil, or mischievous, hastening to do what is not fit, or proper, for him. (TA.) ― -b2- One who rushes headlong into affairs by reason of excessive briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness: (O, L, TA:) thus correctly written; but in the copies of the K, ↓ . (TA.) ― -b3- Lightwitted; weak and stupid; deficient in intellect
; or light and hasty in disposition or deportment. (TA.) ― -b4- And, with p , A woman who transgresses the proper bounds or limits, and is light [ in conduct ]. (TA.)

The mouth of a streamlet or rivulet; (IB, Msb, K;) i. e. a place hollowed out by the water in the side of a river, whence it flows forth: (Msb:) pl. turaEN (IB, Msb) and turoEaAtN and turaEaAtN and turuEaAtN : (Msb:) in the S it is said to signify the mouths of streamlets or rivulets; but correctly the sentence should be, turaEN is pl. of turoEapN , and has this signification. (IB.) ― -b2- A canal, or channel of water, to a meadow or garden or the like: (L, TA:) this is the meaning commonly known [in the present day: the general name in Egypt for a canal cut for the purpose of irrigation, conveying the water of the Nile through the adjacent fields]. (TA.) ― -b3- The opening, or gap, of a wateringtrough or tank, by which the water enters, and where the people draw it: (Az, Mgh, * K, * TA:)

; or, as in the L, the part of the watering-trough or tank which is the station of the drinkers. (TA.) ― -b4- A meadow, or garden, or the like, (S, K,) in an elevated place: (K:) if in low land, it is called rawoDapN . (TA.) ― -b5- A stair

; or a flight of steps by which one ascends; syn. darajapN : (S, K:) so accord. to some in a trad., which see in what follows: (S, * TA:) and particularly the flight of steps of a pulpit. (AA, Sgh, K.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A door, or gate: (S, Sgh, Msb, K:) pl. turaEN . (K.) You say, fataHa turoEapa Ald~aAri (tropical:) He opened the door of the house. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., A_in~a minobariy h`*aA EalaY turoEapK mino turaEi Aljan~api , (S, TA,) as though meaning, (tropical:) Verily this my pulpit is at a gate of the gates of Paradise: thus explained by Sahl Ibn-Saad Es-Sá'idee, the relater of the trad.; and A'Obeyd says, wahuwa Alwajohu [“ and it is the proper, ” or “ the valid and obvious, way, ” of explaining it], meaning that it is the preferable explanation: but the author of t

A torrent filling the valley; as also ↓ : (K:) or a torrent which fills the valley: (S:) and ↓ the latter, a vehement torrent. (TA.) J says, in the S, that ↓ signifies $adiydN ; and he cites the words of a poet thus: faA@fotara$a AlA^aroDa bisayorK A^atoraEaA ascribed by some to El-'Ajjáj, but correctly, accord. to IB, the words of Ru-beh; making two mistakes, in saying Aftr$ , in the sing., and bsyr : moreover, the last word in the citation is a pret. verb: [the right reading is] faA@fotara$uwA AlA^aroDa bisayolK A^atoraEaA [ And they travelled the land with a multitude like a torrent that filled the valleys]: the poet describes the Benoo-Temeem, and their travelling the land like the torrent by reason of multitude. (Sgh, TA.) -A2- (assumed tropical:) A door-keeper. (Th, S, K.)
: see tar~aAEN , in three places.
A filled watering-trough or tank: (TA:) and jafonapN mutoraEapN a filled bowl. (S.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. , (Sgh, K,) inf. n. tarafN , (M, TA,) He enjoyed, or led, a plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life
; or a life of ease and plenty; (M, Sgh, K;) as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b2- And the former verb, (assumed tropical:) It (a plant, or herbage,) was, or became, luxuriant, flourishing, succulent, or sappy
; or bright and fresh, by reason of plentiful irrigation. (M, TA.)
2 see 4, in two places. ― -b2- tatoriyfN [app. as the inf. n. of the pass. verb, tur~ifa , also signifies] Good feeding. (M.) ― -b3- And tr~f Alr~ajula , and ↓ , He rendered the man submissive
; or made him to submit: and he made the man king, or prince: [in both senses] like raf~alahu . (M.)
4 [ Wealth, or what God bestowed upon him, ] made him to behave exorbitantly; to be excessively disobedient or rebellious; to exalt himself, and be inordinate in infidelity

; or to be extravagant in acts of disobedience and in wrongdoing: (S, K:) and so saEapu AlEayo$i [ plentifulness and easiness of life ]: and in like manner, ↓ it caused him to exult, or to exult greatly, or excessively, and to behave insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully. (TA.) And [ Wealth, or what God bestowed upon him, ] made him to enjoy, or lead, a plentiful, and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life
; or a life of ease and plenty; as also ↓ . (K.) ― -b2- Atrf Alr~ajula He gave the man the object of his eager desire
; or of his yearning, or longing, or appetency. (Lh, M.) ― -b3- See also
2. -A2- Atrf also signifies He persevered in, or persisted in, or resolved upon, transgression, wrongdoing, or deviation from the right way. (El-'Ozeyzee, K.)
10 He magnified himself
; or behaved proudly, haughtily, or insolently: he behaved exorbitantly; was excessively disobedient or rebel-lious; exalted himself, and was inordinate in infidelity
; or was extravagant in acts of disobedience and in wrongdoing. (Z, Sgh, K.)
Plentifulness, and pleasantness or easiness, and softness or delicacy, of life; a life of softness or delicacy, and ease, comfort, or affluence
; or ease and plenty; syn. naEomapN , (T, K, TA,) and saEapu AlEayo$i : (TA:) or i. q. niEomapN [i. e. wealth

; or what God bestows upon one; &c.]. (Mgh, and so in the CK. [But this I think a mistranscription, for naEomp .]) ― -b2- Good, sweet, or pleasant, food. (IDrd, M, K.) ― -b3- A new, or strange, thing, ( $aYo'N TariyfN , [in some copies of the K, Zariyf is put in the place of Tariyf ,]) that one appropriates, or peculiarly assigns, [ as a gift ] to a friend
; or by [ the gift of ] which one distinguishes a friend: (K:) any Turofap [i. e. gift not given to any one before
; or of which the recipient did not possess the like, and which pleases him

; or novel, or rare, and pleasing, present ]. (M, TA.) -A2- A thing protuberant in the middle of the upper lip, by nature. (Lth, * T, * S, M, K.) -A3- A misoqaAp [q. v.] with which one drinks. (M, TA.)
Having a natural protuberance in the middle of his upper lip, called turofap . (Lth, * T, * M, K.)

[pass. part. n. of 4, q. v.] One left to do what he will; not prevented from doing so. (Ibn- 'Arafeh, K.) ― -b2- And hence, (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA,) One enjoying, or leading, a plentiful; and a pleasant or an easy, and a soft or delicate, life

; or a life of ease and plenty: (Ibn-'Arafeh, M, K, TA:) luxurious, or indulging himself largely in the pleasures, or delights, of the present life, and in its appetites, or eager desires: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) one who is not prevented from enjoying himself: (K, TA:) and one whose means of subsistence are made ample, or plentiful; as also ↓ : (M:) one whom plentifulness, and pleasantness or easiness, and softness or delicacy, of life, or whom a life of ease and plenty, (T,) or whom wealth, or what God has bestowed upon him, and plentifulness and easiness of life, (Mgh,) causes to exult, or to exult greatly, or excessively, and to behave insolently and unthankfully, or ungratefully: (T, Mgh:) and i. q. jab~aArN [i. e. one who magnifies himself

; or behaves proudly, haughtily, or insolently; &c.]: (K:) so says Katádeh, in explaining the phrase A^amaronaA mutorafiyhaA , in the Kur [xvii. 17: see A^amara ]: or, accord. to some, mtrfyhA here means the worst of its chiefs; and the leaders in evil. (TA.) ― -b3-

senses.text: 1 , (ISk, JK, S, K,) inf. n. taroqaApN , (ISk, S, K,) I hit, or hurt, his (a man's, ISk, JK, S) taroquwap [or collar-bone ]. (ISk, JK, S, K.)

The collar-bone; the bone between the pit at the uppermost part of the chest and the shoulder, (JK, S, Mgh, K,) on either side, connecting those two parts, (JK, Mgh,) of a man &c.; (TA;) each of the two prominent bones in the uppermost part of the chest, from the head of each shoulder to the edge of the pit above mentioned: (TA in art. trb :) [and sometimes, as in a phrase which see below,] the fore part of the Haloq [here app. meaning the throat ], at the uppermost part of the chest, the place into which the soul [for Aln~afasu , in copies of the K, I read Aln~afosu ] rises [ when one is at the point of death ]: (K in art. rqw :) pl. trAqK (JK, Mgh, K) and trAy^iq ; (JK, K;) the latter formed by transposition: (JK:) Fr says that the latter pl. is used by some for the former: (TA:) the sin

, an arabicized word, (S, Msb, K,) from the Greek, (Msb, K,) [i. e. from ,] or originally Persian, (S, O,) also written and pronounced diroyaAqN , (JK, Msb,) and TiroyaAqN ; (Msb;) or, as some say, from Alr~iyqu , because containing the spittle of serpents, and, if so, it is Arabic [in origin]: (Msb:) [ Theriac; also called treacle; ] an antidote for poisons; (S, O;) a certain compound medicine, (K,) comprising many ingredients, at most ninety or ninety-six, and at least sixty-four, (TA,) sometimes including the flesh of vipers, (K, TA,) and that of asses, which cause it to be prohibited and impure, or, as some say, it is prohibited without restriction: (TA:) it is a remedy against the bite or sting of rapacious venomous reptiles and the like, and poisonous potions: (K: [I omit some unprof

Also, and ↓ , (assumed tropical:) Wine; (S, O, K;) because it dispels anxiety; (S;) or because it is a remedy for anxieties; (O;) wherefore it is also termed SaAbuwnu Alhumuwmi . (TA.) tiroyaAqapN : see the last sentence above. [ baA*inojaAnu tiroyaAqiY~N Zanthium. ]

senses.text: 1 , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. tarokN (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and trokaAnN , with kesr, (Fr, K,) He left it, forsook it, relinquished it, abandoned it, deserted it, or quitted it; either intentionally, and by choice, or by constraint, and of necessity: (Er-Rághib, TA:) he left it, forsook it, &c., as above; namely, a thing that he desired, or wished for, and also a thing that he did not desire, or did not wish for: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) he left it, quitted it, went away from it, or departed from it; namely, a place: and he left him, forsook him, relinquished him, abandoned him, deserted him, quitted him, or separated himself from him: (Msb:) he cast it, or threw it, away, as a thing of no account; rejected it; discarded it; cast it off; left it off: (MF, TA:) he left it, left it

; or motionless, in the same state as before thy passing through it, and strike it not with thy rod, nor alter anything thereof; (Bd;) or motionless, parted asunder; (Jel;) so that the Egyptians may enter it; (Bd, Jel;) is an instance of the verb meaning leaving intentionally, and by choice: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and kamo tarakuwA mino jan~aAtK waEuyuwnK , in the next verse, How many gardens and springs did they leave! (Jel,) is an instance of the verb meaning leaving by constraint, and of necessity. (Er-Rághib, TA.) In a phrase such as taraka Haq~ahu , meaning He made his right, or due, or claim, to be null, or he rejected it, and such as taraka rakoEapN mina AlS~alaApi , meaning He neglected, omitted, or left unperformed, a rkEp , of the prayer, [it is said (but I think it doubtful) that] the

76 &c.], (TA,) means And we have perpetuated (K, Jel, TA) to him a eulogy among the later generations (Jel, TA) of the prophets and peoples to the day of resurrection, [namely,] Salutation &c. (Jel.) ― -b3- Alt~aroku is also syn. with AljaEolu , (Lth, K, TA,) in some instances; (Lth, TA;) as though it had two contr. significations: (K:) [i. e.,] when taraka is doubly trans., it has the meaning of Say~ara , (MF, TA,) or jaEala . (TA.) So in the saying, tarakotu AlHabola $adiydFA I made, or rendered, the rope strong

; or made it, or caused it, to be, or become, strong. (TA.) So too in the Kur ii. 16, watarakahumo fiY ZulumaAtK And maketh, or causeth, them to be in darknesses. (Ksh, Bd, MF.) And sometimes one says of any action that has come at last to a certain state, maA tarakotuhu ka*aA [ I did not make it, or cause it, to be thus ]. (TA.) -A2- tarika , aor. , (IAar, K,) inf. n. tarokN , (TK,) He (a man, IAar) married, i. e. took to wife, a tariykap , (IAar, K,) meaning a woman that had remained a virgin, unmarried, until she had become of middle age, or long after she had attained to puberty, in the house, or tent, of her parents. (TA.)

3 [inf. n. mutaArakapN ] is syn. with xaAlaAhu (S in art. xlw ) [which is explained in the K, in art. xlw , as syn. with tarakahu , He left, forsook, relinquished, abandoned, &c., him or it; and thus it may often be well rendered: but it properly signifies he left him, forsook him, &c., being left, &c., by him; whence it is said in the Mgh, in art. wdE , that muwaAdaEapu is syn. with muSaAlaHapN because it is mutaArakapN : Golius, as on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, explains tArkhu as signifying he dismissed him, and did not molest him: he left him unmolested is one of its meanings, but is not the primary signification: accord. to the TK, mtArkp signifies the leaving, &c., anything in the state in which it is: and the leaving, &c., one another ]. One says also, taArakotuhu AlbayoEa , (S, M
6 , (K,) or AlA^amora fiymaA bayonahumo , (Mgh,) They relinquished [ concurrently ], one with another, the affair that was between them. (TK.)
8 : see 1, in five places.
: see tariykapN . -A2- Also A [ drinking-cup or bowl such as is called ] qadaH which a man lifts, or carries, with his two hands. (Ibn-'Abbád, TA.)

A certain nation; (S, Msb, K;) [namely, the Turks: ] turokiY~N is its n. un.: (Msb, TA:) [and signifies also Turkish: ] pl. A^atoraAkN . (Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., AutorukuwA Alt~aroka maA tarakuw kumo [ Leave ye alone the Turks as long as they leave you alone ]. (TA.) [ turokiY~u Alwajohi often occurs in post-classical works as meaning Having a Turkish face; i. e. round-faced, or broad-faced; opposed to EarabiY~u Alwajohi .]

: see tariykapN , in two places. ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A woman such as is termed raboEapN [i. e. of middling stature ]: (Ibn-'Abbád, K:) pl. tarokaAtN . (TA.) ― -b3- It is said in a trad., jaA='a Alxaliylu A_ilaY mak~apa yuTaAliEu tarokatahu (assumed tropical:) [ El-Khaleel (i. e. Abraham) came to Mekkeh to get knowledge of his trkp ], meaning Hagar, and her son Ishmael: (K:) the word originally means an ostrich's egg, and is here used metaphorically; for the ostrich lays but one egg in the year, and then leaves it and goes away: (TA:) Z says, in the Fáïk, that it is thus related, with the r quiescent; (Nh, O, TA;) but it would be a proper way if it were with kesr to the r [↓ ,] as meaning the thing that he had left, or forsaken, &c. (Nh, O, K.)
: see what next follows.

A thing that is left, forsaken, relinquished, abandoned, deserted, or quitted; like TalibapN meaning “ a thing desired, or sought; ” (TA;) see also tarokapN : particularly, the inheritance, or property that is left, of a person deceased; (S, Msb, K; *) also pronounced ↓ : pl. tarikaAtN . (Msb.)

an imperative verbal noun, meaning Autoruko [ Leave thou, &c.]. (S, TA.) Hence the saying, taraAki taraAki SuHobapa AlA^atoraAki [ Leave thou, leave thou, the companionship of the Turks ]. (TA.) Yoo says that taraAka is a dial. var. of the same; but this is only when it is used as a prefixed noun, as in taraAkahaA for taraAkihaA . (TA.)
: see the next paragraph, in two places.

A woman that is left unmarried; (S, K;) that has remained a virgin, unmarried, until she has become of middle age, or long after she has attained to puberty, in the house, or tent, of her parents: (TA:) it is not applied to a male: (Lh, TA:) pl. taraAy^iku . (S.) ― -b2- A meadow the depasturing of which has been neglected: (S, K:) or a pasture-land where people have pastured their beasts, either in a desert or upon a mountain, and of which the beasts have eaten until there remain [ only ] some relics of wood. (TA.) ― -b3- Water left by a torrent: (IB, K:) used in this sense by El-Farezdak. (IB.) ― -b4- An egg after the young bird has gone forth from it: (K:) or an ostrich's egg (S, K) which she forsakes (S, TA) in the desert after it has become empty: (TA:) or, as some say, an ostrich's eg

(Msb.) vaqifahu , aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. vaqofN , (S, K, *) or vaqafN , (Msb,) [but the former is better known,] primarily signifies, He perceived it, or attained it, by knowledge, or by deed: (Bd ii. 187:) or he perceived it, or attained it, by his sight, by expertness in vision: and hence, (Er-Rághib, TA,) (tropical:) he reached him, or overtook him, (IF, Msb, K, and Er-Rághib,) in war, or fight: (Msb:) or (K) (assumed tropical:) he fou

187 &c.:) or (assumed tropical:) he found him in the way of taking and overcoming: (Ksh in ii. 187:) or (K) (assumed tropical:) he took him, or it, (Lth, Msb, K,) namely, a thing: (Msb:) or (K) by implication, (Bd in ii. 187,) (assumed tropical:) he gained the victory, or mastery, over him; overcame him; (IDrd, Msb, K, and Bd ubi suprà;) or got possession of him. (IDrd, Msb, K.) It is said in the Kur [ii.

187 and iv. 93], waA@qotuluwhumo Hayovu vaqifotumuwhumo And slay ye them wherever ye find them: (Ksh, Bd, Jel, TA:) or wherever ye take them, or overcome them, or overtake them. (TA.) And exs. occur also in the Kur [iii.
61 [and lx. 2]. (TA.) For another ex., see 4, below. ― -b4- vaqifahu also signifies He thrust him, or pierced him, [with a spear or the like,] namely, a man. (Ham p.
772.) ― -b5- See also

2 , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. tavoqiyfN , (S, Mgh, K, KL,) He straightened it, or made it even, (S, Mgh, K, KL,) or straightened what was crooked thereof; (Msb;) namely, a spear, (S, KL,) [and a bow, (see viqaAfN ,)] or a crooked thing; with the viqaAf : (Mgh:) [and so ↓ , accord. to an explanation of the inf. n. vaqofN in the KL.] tavoqiyfu Als~ahomi EalaY Alqawosi , as meaning The directing the arrow upon the bow straightly towards the object aimed at, is not approved. (Mgh.) ― -b2-

Hence, (Mgh,) (tropical:) He disciplined him, or educated him well, and amended him, or improved him. (Mgh, TA.) You say, lawolaA tavoqiyfuka watawoqiyfuka maA kunotu $ayoy^FA (tropical:) [ But for thy disciplining, or good educating, and amending, or improving, and thy teaching, I had not been anything ]. (TA.) ― -b3- You say also, of vinegar, yuvaq~ifu AlT~aEaAma , i. e. It makes food acid. (Har p.

3 ↓ , (K,) inf. n. of the former muvaAqafapN and viqaAfN , (TA,) and aor. of the latter , (K,) He vied with him, or strove to surpass him, in skill, (K, TA,) and intelligence, or sagacity, and the perceiving, or attaining, of a thing, and the doing thereof, (TA,) and he surpassed him therein. (K, TA.) Er-Rághib says that this is metaphorical. (TA.) [Accord. to J,] AlmuvaAqafapu is from vaqufa in the first of the senses explained above. (S.) ― -b2- viqaAfN also signifies The contending with another: and particularly in fight, or with the sword: (K: [see also vaqofN , below:]) and the using of, or performing with, the sword; like viqaAfapN . (TA.) And vAqfhu , inf. n. muvaAqafapN , He played with him with the sword, or some other weapon. (TA.)

4 [ I was made to gain the mastery over him, or to overcome him: or, which is virtually the same,] he was appointed for me [ that I might have the mastery over him ]. (Sgh, K.) 'Amr Dhu-l-Kelb says, faA_ino A^uvoqifotumuwniY faA@qotuluwniY fasawofa tarawona baAliY ↓ And if ye [ be made to ] gain the mastery over me, i. e. if it be appointed for you to meet me [ and overcome me ], then slay me: but if I meet [you and overcome ], then shall ye see my condition: but some relate it thus: wamano A^avoqafo , meaning but whom I meet, of you, I will slay him: (Skr, Sgh, TA:) [and J gives it thus:] faA_im~aA tavoqafuwniY Alx [meaning And if ye meet me &c.]. (S.)

5 (tropical:) [ He was, or became, disciplined, or educated well, and amended, or improved; quasipass. of 2, q. v.] You say, halo tavaq~afotu A_il~aA EalaY yadika (tropical:) [ Was I, or have I been, disciplined, &c., save by thy agency, or means? ]. (A, TA.)
6 They contended, or played, one with another, with swords, or other weapons. (TA.)

Skilled, or skilful; and light, active, quick, or sharp; and intelligent, or sagacious; as also ↓ and ↓ (S, K) and ↓ and ↓ : (K:) or ↓ signifies quick in understanding a narration: (Msb:) and ↓ , applied to a woman, intelligent, or sagacious. (K.) You say also rajulN vaqofN laqofN and laqifN ↓ , meaning A man who is a relater, a poet, an archer or a caster of the spear &c.: (Lth, JK, TA:) or light, active, quick, or sharp, and skilful: (S and K in art. lqf :) or quick in understanding what is said to him; and in taking what is thrown to him: or skilful in his art, or handicraft: (TA in that art.:) or a man who keeps, preserves, or guards, and manages, or orders, well, that which he possesses: (ISk, TA:) and Lh adds laqiyfN ↓ : and Ibn-'Abbád, liq~iyfN ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- A man quick in taking
187.) -A2- vaqofN , or (as it is written in one place in the TA) ↓ , also signifies Contention: and particularly in fight, or with the sword: like viqaAfN [inf. n. of 3, q. v.]. (TA.)
: see vaqofN , in two places.

Skill, and intelligence, or sagacity; as also ↓ . (TA.) -A2- Also An instrument with which spears are straightened, (S, K, TA,) and bows also, (TA,) and [ other ] crooked things; (JK, Mgh, TA;) made of iron: (JK, TA:) or a strong piece of wood, a cubit in length, having at its extremity a hole large enough to admit the bow, [ or the spear ], which is inserted into it, and pinched and pressed in the part that requires this to be done until it becomes in the state that is desired; but this is not done to bows nor to spears until they have been greased, and prepared with fire, or exposed thereto so as to have become altered in colour: (AHn, TA:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^avoqifapN and [of mult.] vuqufN . (JK, TA.) ― -b2- [Also The handle of a shield of the kind called Hajafap : see A_ixaA*apN .

: see vaqofN , in three places. ― -b2- Also Very acid; applied to vinegar; (K;) and so ↓ , (S, K,) like Hir~iyfN applied to the onion. (S.) And A^abuw vaqiyfK (tropical:) Vinegar [itself]; so named because it makes food acid. (Har p.
Also, and ↓ , A thing skilled in. (Ham p.
772.) ― -b4- And both these words, A man thrust or pierced [with a spear or the like]. (Ham ibid.)
The use of, or performance with, the sword; like viqaAfN [inf. n. of 3, q. v.]. (TA.) You say, huwa Hasanu Alv~iqaAfapi biAls~ayofi [ He is good in respect of performance with the sword ]. (TA.)
: see viqaAfN .
: see vaqofN , in two places: ― -b2- and see vaqiyfN .
More, and most, skilled, or skilful, [in a general sense, and particularly] in contending, or playing, with the sword, or other weapon. (TA.)
A spear straightened, or made even. (TA.) [Accord. to Freytag, it is poetically used as signifying A spear itself; and so with p .]
: see vaqiyfN .

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. viqalN (S, Msb, K, &c.) and viqolN , a contraction of the former, (Msb,) and vaqaAlapN , (K, TA, in the CK viqAlap , but) like karaAmapN , (TA,) It (a thing, S, Msb) was, or became, heavy, weighty, or ponderous. (S, K.) [See viqalN , below.] ― -b2- See also

4. ― -b3- [(assumed tropical:) It was, or became, heavy, weighty, or preponderant, ideally. ] faA^am~aA mano vaqulato mawaAziynuhu , in the Kur ci. 5, means (assumed tropical:) And as to him whose good deeds shall be preponderant. (Bd, Jel.) [See also Kur vii.

104.] ― -b4- [(assumed tropical:) It was, or became, heavy, or weighty, as meaning onerous, burdensome, oppressive, afflictive, grievous, or troublesome. ] You say, vaqula Alqawolu (tropical:) The saying was [ heavy, or weighty, &c.

; or] unpleasant to be heard. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur vii. 186, vaqulato fiY Als~am`waAti waAlA^aroDi (assumed tropical:) It (the time of the resurrection) will be momentous, or formidable, [ in the heavens and on the earth, or] to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, (Bd, Jel,) to the angels and men and genii; app. alluding to the wisdom shown in concealing it: (Bd:) or it means the knowledge thereof [ is difficult ]: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) or it is occult, or hidden. (Kt, TA.) [ vaqula is also said of a word, and of a sound, meaning (assumed tropical:) It was heavy, or not easy, of utterance
; or heavy to the ear: see

2. And of an affair, or action, meaning (assumed tropical:) It was afflictive, grievous, troublesome, or difficult. In these and similar senses, it is trans. by means of EalaY : you say, vaqula Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, heavy, weighty, onerous, &c., to him. In like manner also it is said of food, meaning (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, heavy to the stomach; difficult of digestion. ] You say also, vaqula samoEuhu (tropical:) [ His hearing was, or became, heavy

; or] his hearing partially went. (K, TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, heavy in sickness, or disease: [and in like manner, in his sleep:] the verb is thus, with damm to the q ; though said in the K to be vaqila , like fariHa , as meaning his disease became violent; (Fet-h el-Báree, TA;) not improbably through error or inadvertence. (MF.) ― -b6- [(assumed tropical:) He was, or became, heavy, slow, sluggish, indolent, lazy, dull, torpid, or drowsy; wanting in alacrity, activity, agility, animation, spirit, or intelligence; stupid. ] You say, yavoqulu Eano qubuwli maA yuloqaY A_ilayohi (assumed tropical:) [ He is averse from receiving, or accepting, or admitting, or is slow to receive, &c., what is said to him ]. (TA.) ― -b7-

Also, said of the Earofaj , and of the vumaAm , (tropical:) Its shoots became luxuriant, or succulent, or sappy. (K, TA.) -A2- vaqalahu , (JK, S, K,) biyadihi , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. vaqolN , (K,) He tried the weight of it, (JK, S, K,) namely, a thing, (K,) or a sheep or goat, (S,) by lifting it [ with his hand ] to see if it were heavy or light. (S, TA.) ― -b2- vaqala Al$~aYo'u Al$~aYo'a fiY Alwazoni , aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) The thing surpassed the thing in weight; outweighed it. (PS.) ― -b3- See also

2 , inf. n. tavoqiylN , He, or it, made it, or him, vaqiyl [i. e. heavy, properly and tropically]: (K:) tvqyl is the contr. of taxofiyfN ; (S;) and signifies the making heavy in weight [&c.]; as also vaqolN [inf. n. of ↓ ]. (KL.) ― -b2- [
Hence, (assumed tropical:) He made it (a word or a sound) heavy, or not easy, of utterance

; or heavy to the ear: and particularly a word by uttering hemzeh with its true, or proper, sound, which is commonly termed taHoqiyqu Alhamozapi , and opposed to taxofiyfuhaA ; and by making a single consonant double; and by making a quiescent consonant movent: often occurring in these senses in lexicons and grammars: opposed to xaf~afahu .]

4 He, or it, (a load, S, or a thing, Msb,) [ burdened him: or] burdened him heavily: (K:) or beyond his power; overburdened him. (JK, Msb, TA. *) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) In the latter sense, said also of a debt: and of sickness, or a disease: (JK:) or, said of sickness, or a disease, and of sleep, and of meanness, or sordidness, (tropical:) it [ burdened him, ] overcame him, and rendered him heavy. (K, * TA, * TK.) -A2- Avqlt , said of a woman, She became gravid; her burden became heavy in her belly: (S:) or she had a burden, (Akh, S, and Bd in vii. 189,) by reason of the greatness of the child in her belly: (Bd, Jel:) or her pregnancy became apparent, or manifest; as also ↓ . (K.)

6 [ tvAql EalaY $aYo'K He pressed heavily, or bore his weight, upon a thing: see mutavaAqilN .] ― -b2- tvAqlwA (assumed tropical:) [ They were heavy, sluggish, or spiritless: ] they did not rise and hasten to the fight when commanded to do so. (IDrd, K.) And tvAql A_ilaY AlA^aroDi , (S and K in art. ArD , &c.,) and Aiv~aAqala AlY AlrD , the former being the original form of the verb, (Bd and Jel in ix. 38,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, heavy, slow, or sluggish, (Bd, Jel,) averse from warring against the unbelievers, (Jel,) and inclining to the earth, or ground; (Bd, Jel;) or propending thereto. (Bd.) And Aiv~aAqala A_ilaY Ald~unoyaA (assumed tropical:) He propended to the present world. (TA.) And tvAql Eanohu (assumed tropical:) He was heavy, or sluggish, and held back from it. (
10 contr. of Aisotaxaf~ahu ; (S and K and TA in art. xf ;) He deemed it, or him, vaqiyl [i. e. heavy, properly and tropically]. (TA in that art.) ― -b2- [
Hence, (assumed tropical:) He deemed it (a word or a sound) heavy, or not easy, of utterance

; or heavy to the ear: often occurring in this sense in lexicons and grammars.] ― -b3- Ausotuvoqila nawomFA (assumed tropical:) [ He was overcome, and rendered heavy, by sleep: and in like manner, maraDFA , by sickness or disease: and luw^omFA , by meanness or sordidness: see its pass. part. n., below]. (JK.)

Weight: or a weight: syn. wazonN : (S, Msb, KL:) pl. A^avoqaAlN . (S.) So in the phrase A^aEoTihi viqolahu [ Give thou him his, or its, weight ]. (S, Msb.) See also mivoqaAlN . You say also, A^aloqaY Ealayohi viqolahu or ↓ [ He threw upon him his weight: see mivoqaAlN , last sentence: and see jiromN ]. (S in art. Awq &c., accord. to different copies.) ― -b2- And A load, or burden: (KL:) or a heavy load or burden: pl. as above. (K.) wataHomilu A^avoqaAlakumo , in the Kur xvi. 7, means And they carry your loads, or burdens; (Bd;) or your heavy loads or burdens. (TA.) ― -b3- A^avoqaAlN (as pl. of viqolN , K, or of ↓ , Bd) also signifies (tropical:) The treasures, or buried treasures, of the earth: and its dead, or corpses. (K, TA, and Bd and Jel in xcix.

2.) ― -b4- Also (as pl. of viqolN , K) (tropical:) Sins. (JK, K.) So in the saying in the Kur [xxix. 12], walayaHomilun~a A^avoqaAlahumo waA^avoqaAlFA maEa A^avoqaAlihimo (tropical:) [ And they shall assuredly bear their sins, and sins (of others whom they have seduced) with their sins ]. (TA.)

A thing, or things, that a man has with him, of such things as burden him: (Ham p. 295:) [and particularly] the household-goods, or furniture and utensils, (El-Fárábee, JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K, Ham ubi suprà, and Bd in xcix. 2,) and (accord. to El-Fárábee, Msb) the household and kindred and party, or domestics, or servants, (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K, and Ham,) of a man, (Ham,) or of a traveller: (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K:) [or the travelling-apparatus and baggage and train, of a man:] pl. A^avoqaAlN ; (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K; *) with which ↓ is syn., (JK, S, K,) as are also ↓ and ↓ and ↓ and ↓ ; (K;) as meaning all the household-goods or furniture and utensils of persons going on a journey. (S, K.) ― -b2- See also viqolN . ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) The requisites and apparatus, instruments, tools, or the like

Heaviness; weight, or weightiness; ponderousness; gravity; contr. of xif~apN : (S, K, and Er-Rághib:) and preponderance: in its primary acceptation, relating to corporeal objects: then, to ideal objects. (Er-Rághib, TA. [See vaqula , throughout.]) See also viqolN . ― -b2- fiY A^u*unihi viqalN (tropical:) [ In his ear is a heaviness, or dulness, ] is said of him whose hearing is not good; as though he were averse from receiving, or accepting, or admitting, or slow to receive, &c., what is said to him. (TA.)

: see vaqalN . ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A fit of drowsiness, or of slumber, that overcomes one: (JK, M, K:) and (tropical:) a heaviness experienced in the chest, (K, TA,) or in the body, (TA,) from food: as also ↓ : (K, TA:) or the former, or ↓ the latter, (accord. to different copies of the S,) (assumed tropical:) a heaviness and languor in the body: (S:) and ↓ the latter, (assumed tropical:) a heaviness that is experienced on the heart. (JK.)
: see vaqalN : ― -b2- and see vaqolapN , in three places.
: see vaqiylN , in two places. ― -b2-
Also, applied to a woman, (JK, S, K,) Heavy; (S;) large in the hinder part, or posteriors: (JK, * S, * K, TA:) or heavy (K, TA) in an ideal sense. (TA.)
: see vaqiylN .

part. n. of vaqula ; (S, Msb, K;) Heavy, weighty, or ponderous: (S, K, and Er-Rághib:) and so in relation to another thing; preponderant: primarily applied to a corporeal thing: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and ↓ and ↓ signify the same: (K:) pl. viqaAlN and vuqolN and vuqalaA='u [which last, however, seems to be applied only to rational beings, agreeably with analogy]. (K.) ― -b2- [Like its verb,] it is also applied to an ideal thing. (Er-Rághib, TA.) [Thus it signifies (assumed tropical:) Heavy, or weighty, in the sense of onerous, burdensome, oppressive, afflictive, grievous, or troublesome: momentous, or formidable: difficult: heavy, or not easy, of utterance

; or heavy to the ear; applied to a word and a sound; and particularly to a word in which a single consonant is made double, and to one in which a quiescent consonant is made movent, like ↓ : heavy to the stomach; difficult of digestion: heavy applied to the hearing: see the verb.] qawolFA vaqiylFA , in the Kur [lxxiii. 5], means (assumed tropical:) A heavy, or weighty, saying. (TA.) Aln~uwnu Alv~aqiylapu means (assumed tropical:) [ The heavy-sounding n ; as in yafoEalan~a &c.;] the contr. of Alxafiyfapu . (TA in art. xf .) ― -b3- It is also applied to a man, (JK,) meaning (tropical:) [ Heavy in sickness, or disease

; or] suffering a violent disease: (K:) [and (assumed tropical:) heavy, slow, sluggish, indolent, lazy, dull, torpid, or drowsy; wanting in alacrity, activity, agility, animation, spirit, or intelligence; stupid: ] and so is ↓ : (JK:) which also means, particularly, (assumed tropical:) overcome, and rendered heavy, by sleep ( nawomFA ), (JK, * K, * TK,) and by sickness or disease ( maraDFA ), and by meanness or sordidness ( luw^omFA ). (K.) viqaAlu Aln~aAsi [expressly said in the TA to be with kesr, but in the CK, erroneously, vuqAl ,] and vuqalaA='u AlnAs mean (assumed tropical:) Those men whose company is disliked; (K;) whom others deem heavy: each is pl. of vaqiylN . (TA.) One says, A^anota vaqiylN EalaY julasaAy^ika (assumed tropical:) [ Thou art heavy, or dull, or unwelcome, to thy co

A deenár of full weight; (Z;) not deficient: (S, K:) pl. vawaAqilu . (S, Z, K.) ― -b2- A^aSobaHa vaAqilFA (assumed tropical:) He became, or became in the morning, heavy by reason of sickness, or disease. (Aboo-Nasr, K, TA.)
More [and most ] heavy. (TA.)

Heavily burdened: (TA:) or burdened beyond his power; overburdened. (JK, TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) Weighed down, or oppressed, by sickness, or disease, (JK,) and by debt. (JK, Er-Rághib.) ― -b3- See also vaqiylN .
, applied to a woman, Gravid; whose burden has become heavy in her belly: (S:) or whose pregnancy has become apparent, or manifest. (K.)
: see vaqiylN . ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Ill received; disapproved; not rendered an object of love to hearts. (Ham p.
A stone of marble; (JK;) a piece of marble by which a carpet is made heavy: (K:) by rule it should be with kesr to the q . (TA.)
The weight ( miyzaAn , JK, S, K, or wazon , Msb, TA, and Jel in iv.

62 and xxi. 48, or zinap , TA) of a thing, (JK, S, Msb, K,) of the like thereof ( mino mivolihi [but why this is added I do not see]); (S, Msb, K;) [i. e.] its equal in weight; (PS, and Bd in x. 62;) its quantity ( miqodaAr ). (Bd in xxi.

48.) maA yaEozubu Eano rab~ika mino mivoqaAli *ar~apK , in the Kur x. 62, means There is not hidden from thy Lord aught of the weight of the smallest ant: (Jel:) or a thing equal in weight to a small ant

; or to the motes that are seen in a ray of the sun that enters through an aperture. (Bd.) ― -b2- A thing with which one weights; as also ↓ ; i. e., any of the weights of the balance. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b3- A certain weight, of which the quantity is well known; (JK;) a dirhem and three sevenths of a dirhem; (Msb, and K in art. mk ;) i. e., the seventh part of ten dirhems: (Msb:) or [ a dirhem and a half; so in the present day; i. e.,] seventy-two sha'eerehs: (El-Karmánee, TA:) or twenty keeráts. (Hidáyeh, TA.) ― -b4- [ A certain coin; ] i. q. diynaArN , q. v.; (Msb in art. dnr ;) a mivoqaAl of gold: pl. mavaAqiylu . (S, K.) ― -b5- A^aloqaY Ealayohi mavaAqiylahu He threw upon him his weight, or burden; syn. maw^uwnatahu [perhaps meaning the burden of supporting him ]. (Aboo-Nasr, S, K.) [S
Bearing one's weight upon a thing: whence the saying, waTiy^ahu waToA^apa AlmutavaAqili [ He trod upon him, or it, with the tread of him who bears his weight, or presses heavily ]. (TA.)
: see vaqiylN .

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. vakalN , (S, Msb,) or vukolN , (Mgh,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) and vakolN , (Mgh,) [or this last is also a simple subst.,] She (a mother) lost him, or became bereft of him; namely, her child, (S, Mgh, Msb,) by death: (Mgh:) and vakilahu , aor. , (K,) inf. n. vakalN , (TA,) he lost him; namely, a friend, or person beloved, or a child. (K.) vakilatoka A^um~uka [lit. meaning May thy mother be bereft of thee ] is an imprecation against him to whom it is addressed, not said with the desire of its having effect, but on an occasion of vehement love, like laA A^abaA laka , [and qaAtalaka A@ll~`hu ,] &c. (Har p.

4 A state of bereavement clave to her; (K;) namely, a woman: or she became in a state of bereavement. (TA.) -A2- A^avokalahaA A@ll~`hu waladahaA God made her to be bereft of her child [ by death ]. (Msb, K.) And Avklhu A@ll~`hu A^um~ahu God made him to be bereft of his mother [ by death ]. (S.)
: see what next follows.

The loss, or the state of being bereft, of a child [ by death ], (S, Msb, K,) or of a friend, or person beloved; (K;) i. e., a woman's loss of her child; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ [which is the inf. n. by general consent], (S, K,) and ↓ . (TA.) It is said in a prov., AlEuquwqu vukolu mano lamo yavokalN [ Undutiful treatment of a parent is (like) the bereavement of him who is not (really) bereft of his child ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Death: and a state of perdition or destruction. (K.)
; fem. vakolaY and vakolaAnapN : see vaAkilN .
: see vaAkilN . ― -b2- falaApN vakuwlN (tropical:) A desert in which the traveller becomes lost. (K, TA.)

, applied to a man, Bereft of a child, or of a friend, or person beloved; as also ↓ or vakolaAnN [with or without tenween, as is shown by the two forms of the fem. mentioned in what follows, but generally without]: (K:) and applied to a woman; (S, Msb, K;) and sometimes vaAkilapN ; (Msb;) as also vakolaY (S, Msb, K) and vakolaAnapN , (IAar, K,) which is rare, (K,) and ↓ ; (S, K;) meaning bereft of her child [ by death ]; (S, Msb;) pl. The name of the letter v , q. v.; as also vaA : pl. [of the former,] vaA='aAtN ; and [of the latter,] A^avowaA='N and A^avoyaA='N . (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np .) -A2- It also stands for vanaA='N , and vawaAbN , and the like. (Idem ubi suprà.) -A3- Also The best of anything; as, for instance, of wheat, and of flesh-meat, and of sugar. (Kh, TA ubi suprà.)
and vaAwiY~N rel. ns. of vaA='N and vaA , the names of the letter v ; as also vayawiY~N . (TA ubi suprà.)

senses.text: 1 , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yavuwbu , (S, Mgh, &c.,) inf. n. vawobN (S, M, Msb, K) and vawabaAnN (S) and vuw^uwbN , (M, K,) He, or it, (a thing, M,) returned; (M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ , inf. n. tavowiybN : (M, K:) he returned to a place to which he had come before

; or it returned &c.: (T:) he (a man) returned, after he had gone away. (S.) You say, tafar~aquwA vum~a vaAbuwA i. e. [ They became separated, or dispersed: then ] they returned. (A.) ― -b2- vAb A_ilaY A@ll~`hi , like taAba , (assumed tropical:) He returned [ from disobedience ] to obedience to God; he repented; as also A^anaAba . (T.) ― -b3- vAb also signifies (assumed tropical:) He returned to a state of advertency, or vigilance

; or he had his attention roused. (Th, T.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) He returned to a state of health, or soundness: (TA, from a trad.:) he became convalescent, and fat, after leanness. (Mgh.) And vAb jisomuhu , (M, A, K,) inf. n. vawabaAnN ; (M, K;) and jisomuhu ↓ ; (IKt, M;) and vAb A_ilayohi jisomuhu ; (T, M, A;) and ↓ , alone; (S, M, A;) (tropical:) He became fat, after leanness; (A;) his good state of body returned to him; (S, M, K; *) his condition of body became good, after extenuation; and health, or soundness, thereof returned to him. (T.) ― -b5- vAb A_ilayohi Eaqoluhu (tropical:) [ His reason, or intellect, returned to him ]: and Hilomuhu [ his forbearance, or clemency ]. (A.) ― -b6- vAb AlmaA='u (assumed tropical:) The water of a well returned, or collected again: (T:) the

2 , inf. n. tavowiybN : see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- vwab baEoda xaSaASapK (tropical:) [ He returned to a state of richness, or competence, after poverty, or straitness, or being in an evil condition ]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- tavowiybN meaning The calling, or summoning, (M, Mgh, K,) to prayer, (M, K,) and to other things, (M,) is said to be from vawobN “ a garment, ” (Mgh,) because a man, when he comes crying out for aid, makes a sign with his garment, (M, Mgh,) moving it about, raising his hand with it, in order that he to whom he calls may see it, (Mgh,) and this action is like a calling, or summoning, (M, Mgh,) and an announcing, to him; so the calling, or summoning, by reason to frequent usage of this word [as meaning the making a sign with a garment ], came to be thus called; and one said o

; or qaAmato qaAmato . (Mgh.) It also signifies The A_iqaAmap ; (Mgh, K, TA;) [meaning, the chanting, by the mubal~iguwn , in a mosque, not by the muw^a*~in , the common words of the A^a*aAn , with the addition of qado qaAmati AlS~alaAho ( The time of prayer has come ), pronounced twice after HY~ ElY AlflAH ;] i. e. the AqAmp of prayer: (IAth, TA:) and this is what is meant by the phrase, in a trad., A_i*aA vuw~iba biAlS~alaApi [ When the words of the AqAmp are chanted ]. (IAth, Mgh, TA.) And The praying after the prayer divinely ordained. (Yoo, T, K.) You say, vw~b , meaning He performed a supererogatory prayer after the prescribed; tvwyb being only after the prescribed; being the praying after praying: (T:) and ↓ signifies the same. (K.) And v~wb birakoEatayoni He performed two rek'ahs a

4 : see 1, in two places. ― -b2- It may also mean (assumed tropical:) It (a valley, or a well,) had a return of water after a stoppage thereof. (Ham p.

598.) -A2- AvAb A@ll~`hu jisomahu (tropical:) God restored him to fatness, after leanness; (A;) restored his body to a good state, or condition. (TA.) ― -b2- A_in~a Eamuwda Ald~iyni laA yuvaAbu biAln~isaA='a A_ino maAla (assumed tropical:) Verily the column of the religion cannot be set upright again by women, if it incline: said by Umm-Selemeh to 'Áïsheh, when the latter desired to go forth to El-Basrah. (T, L.) ― -b3- AvAbhu A@ll~`hu , (T, S, * M, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ivaAbapN ; (Mgh;) and A^avowabahu [dev. from rule]; (M, K;) and ↓ , (T, A,) inf. n. tvowiybN ; (T, Mgh;) God recompensed, compensated, requited, or rewarded, him: (T, S, * M, A, Mgh, * Msb, K:) said in relation to good and to evil. (T.) And AvAbhu , (Lh, M,) and A^avowabahu , (T,) mavuwbapF HasanapF , (Lh, T, M,) and mavow

6 : see vuy^iba , in art. vA^b .

10 He restored to himself, or repossessed himself of, property; syn. AisotarojaEahu ; (T, A, K;) his property having gone away. (T, A.) And Aisotavabotu bimaAlika I restored to myself, or repossessed myself of, property, by means of that which thou gavest me; my property having gone away. (A.) El-Kumeyt says, A_in~a AlEa$iyrapa tasotaviybu bimaAlihi fayugiyru wahowa muwaf~irN A^amowaAlahaA [ Verily the tribe restore to themselves wealth by means of his property; and he makes incursions into hostile territories at his own expense, making their property abundant by the spoil that they gain with him]. (T, TA.) ― -b2- AstvAbhu He asked him to recompense, compensate, requite, or reward, him. (S, K.)

A garment, (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) [or piece of cloth or stuff, ] that is worn by men, composed of linen, cotton, wool, fur, xaz~ [q. v.], (Mgh, Msb,) silk, or the like; (Msb;) but [properly] not what is cut out of several pieces, such as the shirt, and trousers, or drawers, &c.; (Mgh;) [though often applied to a shirt or shift ( qamiyS or diroE ) and to a jub~ap &c.:] it seems to be so called because the wearer returns to it, or it to the wearer, time after time: (Mgh:) [also a garment worn by women and girls over the shift; (see A^uSodapN ;) app., as in the present day, a long gown, reaching to the feet, with very wide sleeves: ] pl. viyaAbN [the pl. of mult.] (T, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and A^avowaAbN [a pl. of pauc.] (S, M, Msb, K) and A^avowubN and A^avow^ubN , (S, M, K,) the last two being p

63.) ― -b5- And A^avowaAbN is sometimes employed to signify (assumed tropical:) The wearers of garments; the wearers' bodies. (R, TA.) Esh-Shemmákh says, (T,) or Leylà, describing camels, (TA,) wamawohaA biA^avowaAbK xifaAfK falaA taraY lahaA $abahFA A_il~aA Aln~aEaAma Almunaf~araA i. e. They mounted them, namely, the travellingcamels, (T,) with their [ light, or agile, ] bodies: [ and thou seest not anything like them, except ostriches scared away. ] (T, TA.) And in like manner, also, the dual is employed to signify (assumed tropical:) The wearer's body, or self

; or what the garments infold: and viyaAb is employed in the same manner. (TA.) You say, lil~hi vawobaAhu , i. e. (tropical:) To God be he [meaning his excellence ] attributed! [for nothing but what is excellent is to be attributed to God:] (A:) or it means lil~hi dar~uhu [ To God be attributed the good that hath proceeded from him! or his good deed! &c.: see arts. Alh and dr ]. (K.) And fiY vawobaYo A^abiY A^ano A^afiyahu meaning (tropical:) [ On me and on my father it rests, or lies, or be it, that I pay it: or] fiY*im~atiY wa*im~apiA^abiY [ on my responsibility and the responsibility of my father ]. (K, TA.) And Ausolulo viyaAbaka mino viyaAbiY (tropical:) Withdraw, or separate, thyself from me. (A.) ― -b6- [The following exs. are mostly, or all, tropical.] ― -b7- A_in~i Almay~ita layub

; or pure in heart, or conduct, or reputation ]. (TA in art. nSH .) And danisu Alv~iyaAbi (tropical:) Vicious, or faulty: (A:) or perfidious: (Fr, T:) or foul, or evil, in reputation, (T, TA,) in conduct, or actions, and in the way that he follows [ with respect to religion and morality ]. (TA.) ― -b10- kalaAbisi vawobaYo zuwrK : see muta$ab~iEN . ― -b11- A^aEoraDa vawobu Almalobasi and Almilobasi &c.: see EaruDa . ― -b12- vawobu AlmaA='i (assumed tropical:) [ The membrane called ] Als~alaY and Algirosu . (K. See these two words.)
: see vaAy^ibN , in two places.

The place where the water collects in a valley or low ground; so called because the water returns to it: (Aboo-Kheyreh, T:) and the middle of a watering-trough or tank, (T, S, M,) to which the water returns when it has been emptied, (S,) or to which what remains of the water returns; (T;) as also ↓ : (S:) the p is a substitute for the w , the medial radical, which is suppressed; (S, L;) the word being from vaAba , aor. yavuwbu : (L:) Aboo-Is-hák infers that this is the case from its having for its dim. ↓ : but it may be from vab~ayotu “ I collected together: ” (M:) it is mentioned in the K in art. vbY or vbw , and not here. (TA.) See also art. vbw or vbY . ― -b2- Also A company of men; (T, M, L;) and so A^uvobiy~apN : (M:) or a company of men in a state of separation or dispersion; (T;) a
Hence, in the Kur [iv. 73], faA@nofiruwA vubaAtK , i. e. [ And go ye forth to to war against the unbelievers] in troops, (Fr, T,) or in distinct bodies. (Yoo, T.) See, again, art. vbw or vbY .
: see vuw^abaA='u , in art. vA^b .

(T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ (T, Msb) and ↓ (T, S, M, K) and ↓ , (EtTemeemee, T, M, K,) the last anomalous, (M,) and unknown to the Kilábees, who knew the second of these words, (T,) A recompense, compensation, requital, or reward, (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) of obedience [ to God ]: (S:) or absolutely; for good and for evil; as appears from the words of the Kur, halo vuw~iba Alkuf~aAru [cited above, see 4]; but more especially and frequently, for good. (IAth, L, MF, TA.) ― -b2- vawaAbN is also used as a quasi-inf. n., in the sense of A_ivaAbapN ; and in this case, accord to the Koofees and Baghdádees, it may govern as a verb, [like the inf. n.,] as in the saying, liA_an~a vawaAba A@ll~hi kul~a muwaH~idK jinaAnN mina Alfirodawosi fiyhaA yuxal~adu [ For God's rewarding every believer in his uni

, [like say~idN ; originally vawiybN , or vayowibN ; i. e.] of the measure faEiylN , (Mgh,) or fayoEilN ; (Msb;) A woman who has become separated from her husband (Lth, T, M, Mgh, K) in any manner: (Lth, T, M, Mgh:) or a woman whose husband has died, or who has been divorced, and has then returned to the marriage-state: (AHeyth, TA:) or one that is not a virgin: (IAth, TA:) or a woman to whom a man has gone in; and a man who has gone in to a woman: (Ks, ISk, S, Mgh, K:) or a person who has married: (Msb:) applied to a man and to a woman; (As, S, M, Msb;) like bikorN and A^ay~imN : (Mgh, Msb:) from vaAba ; (IAth, Mgh, Msb;) because they generally return time after time to the marriage-state: (Mgh:) but mostly applied to a woman; because she returns to her family in a manner different from t

and vuyuwbapN , as meaning The state of being a vay~ib , are not of the genuine language of the Arabs. (Mgh.)
One who takes care of the clothes in the bath. (K.) [A post-classical word.]

i. q. taw~aAbN [One who repents, or returns from disobedience to obedience to God, much or often ]. (T.) -A2- A seller of garments, or pieces of cloth: (AZ, T, L, K:) and a possessor thereof. (Sb, S, L, K.)

(tropical:) A well into which water returns after one has drawn from it; (A, TA;) see mavaAbN ; and in like manner, [but in an intensive sense in the second of the following phrases,] ↓ , and waEiybK ↓ [in which wEyb is an epithet]: (T, L, TA:) or the first of these three phrases means a well of which the water stops sometimes, and then returns. Hence, kalaA^N mivolu vaAy^ibi AlbaHori (assumed tropical:) Fresh, sappy, [ green, ] herbage. (T, L.) ― -b3- qawomN lahumo vaAy^ibN (tropical:) A people, or number of men, who come company after company. : see mavaAbapN , in four places: ― -b2- and see vubipN . ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The place from which the water returns [ to supply the place of that which has been drawn, in a well ]: whence ↓ [see vaAy^ibN ]. ; or a house; because the inhabitants thereof return to it (ISh, S) after having gone to their affairs: (S:) the pl. is mavaAbaAtN ; [also mentioned above as pl. of mavaAbN ;] (ISh;) or it is ↓ ; (S;) [or this is a coll. gen. n.;] or, accord. to Fr and others, mavaAabapN and ↓ are the same: Th says that a house, or tent, ( bayot ,) is called mavaAbapN ; and some say ↓ ; but no one reads thus [in the Kur]. (TA.) It has the first of all these meanings in the Kur ii. 119: (T, S, Bd, Jel, TA:) or it there means a place of recompense or reward for the pilgrimage to the Kaabeh and the visitation thereof. (Bd.) ― -b2- And, sometimes, The place where the hunter, or fowler, puts his snare. (S.) ― -b3- mavaAbapN Albiy^ori (tropical:) The place where the water of the well collects: (A, TA:) or the pl

and muvay~ibN : see vay~ibN .

senses.text: 1 and both signify He, or it, sank into the ground; and Yaakoob asserts that the v in the former is a substitute for the s in the latter. (L, TA.) You say, vaAxato qadamuhu biAlwaHoli , (S,) or fiY AlwaHoli , (L,) aor. tavuwxu and taviyxu , His foot sank, or entered, into the mire. (S, L.) And vaAxati AlA_iSobaEu , aor. as above, (L, K,) inf. n. vawoxN , (L,) The finger entered, or sank, into a swollen, or tumid, or a soft, or yielding, substance; (L, K;) as also saAxat , (L,) and taAxat : (Lth:) but this last is disapproved by IDrd, and J and others do not mention it. (TA in art. twx .)

senses.text: 1 , aor. yavuwru , (M,) inf. n. vaworN and vuw^uwrN and vawaraAnN , (M, K,) It (a thing, M) became raised, roused, excited, stirred up, or provoked; syn. haAja ; (M;) syn. of the inf. n. hayajaAnN : (K:) as also ↓ . (M, K.) ― -b2- Said of dust, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb,) and of smoke, (M, A,) and of other things, (M, TA,) inf. n. vaworN and vuw^uwrN (S, M, Msb, K) and vawaraAnN , (K,) (tropical:) It became raised, or stirred up; (Mgh, Msb;) and spread: (Mgh:) or rose, (S, M, A, K,) and appeared; (M;) as also ↓ : (K:) also said of the redness in the sky after sunset, inf. n. vaworN and vawaraAnN , (tropical:) it spread upon the horizon, and rose: (TA: [see vaworN :]) and vAr , said of anything, means (assumed tropical:) it appeared and spread. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Said of a camel lying upon his breast,

Also, (S, M,) inf. ns. as first mentioned above, (M, K,) He leaped, or sprang; (M, K;) as also ↓ . (K.) You say, vAr A_ilayohi He leaped, or sprang, to, or towards, him, or it. (M.) And vArbihi Aln~aAsu The people leaped, or sprang, upon him. (S.) And vAr A_ilaY Al$~ar~i He rose, or hastened, to do evil, or mischief. (Msb.) ― -b6- vAr AlmaA='u The water flowed forth with force; gushed forth. (TA.) ― -b7- vAr bihi Ald~amu , (TA,) inf. ns. as first mentioned above, (K,) (tropical:) The blood appeared in him; as also ↓ . (K, * TA.) And vAr Ald~amu fiY wajohahi (tropical:) The blood appeared in [or mantled in or mounted into ] his face; as also ↓ . (M.) ― -b8- vArt bihi AlHaSobapu , (S, M, A,) inf. n. vaworN and vuw^uwrN and vawaArN [or vuwaArN ?] and vawaraAnN , (M,) (tropical:) The measles s

; or became agitated by a tendency to vomit; syn. ja$aA^atN , (T, S,) i. e. AirotafaEato ; (T;) or jaA$ato , (TA,) i. e. faAratN . (T.) ― -b12- vAr AlgaDabu , (Msb,) inf. n. vaworN , (M,) (assumed tropical:) [ Anger became roused, or excited, or inflamed: or became roused, or excited in the utmost degree: or boiled: or spread: (see vaAy^rN , below:) or] became sharp. (M, Msb.) ― -b13- vArt bayonahumo fitonapN wa$ar~N (A, Msb *) (tropical:) Discord, or dissension, or the like, and evil, or mischief, became excited among them, or between them. (Msb.)

2 see 4, in three places. ― -b2- You say also, vw~r AlA^amora , inf. n. tavowiyrN , (assumed tropical:) He searched, or sought, for, or after, the thing, or affair; inquired, or sought information, respecting it; searched, or inquired, into it; investigated, scrutinized, or examined, it. (M.) And vw~r AlquroA=na (assumed tropical:) He searched after a knowledge of the Kur-án, (S, K,) or its meanings: (M:) or he read it, and inquired of, or examined, diligently, those skilled in it, respecting its interpretation and meanings: (Sh:) or he scrutinized it, and meditated upon its meanings, and its interpretation, and the reading of it. (TA.)

415.) -A2- A piece, (T, S, Mgh, Msb,) or large piece, (M, K,) of A^aqiT , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) i. e. milk which [ has been churned and cooked and then left until it ] has become congealed and hard like stone: (TA:) pl. TuHolubN , (AZ, T, S, M, Msb, K,) and EaromaDN , and galofaqN ; (M;) and the like thereof: (T, M:) and small rubbish, or broken particles of things, (Msb, TA,) or anything, (K,) upon the surface of water, (Msb, K, TA,) which the pastor beats to make the water clear for the bulls or cows. 1 , (S, M, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. tarokN (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and trokaAnN , with kesr, (Fr, K,) He left it, forsook it, relinquished it, abandoned it, deserted it, or quitted it; either intentionally, and by choice, or by constraint, and of necessity: (Er-Rághib, TA:) he left it, forsook it, &c., as above; namely, a thing that he desired, or wished for, and also a thing that he did not desire, or did not wish for: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) he left it, quitted it, went away from it, or departed from it; namely, a place: and he left him, forsook him, relinquished him, abandoned him, deserted him, quitted him, or separated himself from him: (Msb:) he cast it, or threw it, away, as a thing of no account; rejected it; discarded it; cast it off; left it off: (MF, TA:) he left it, left it

; or motionless, in the same state as before thy passing through it, and strike it not with thy rod, nor alter anything thereof; (Bd;) or motionless, parted asunder; (Jel;) so that the Egyptians may enter it; (Bd, Jel;) is an instance of the verb meaning leaving intentionally, and by choice: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and kamo tarakuwA mino jan~aAtK waEuyuwnK , in the next verse, How many gardens and springs did they leave! (Jel,) is an instance of the verb meaning leaving by constraint, and of necessity. (Er-Rághib, TA.)
